newsitem.title: USA: Cleveland State University bonds single-A by S&P.
newsitem.headline: Cleveland State University bonds single-A by S&P.

text.p: Standard & Poor's today has assigned its single-A' rating to Cleveland State University, Ohio's general receipts bonds series 1996.

The rating is based on the university's role as one of Ohio's 13 publicly supported colleges and universities, improving financial performance and liquidity, and manageable debt burden. Offsetting factors include recent enrollment declines, open admissions, and a narrow geographic draw.

The university is an urban, primarily commuter school located in downtown Cleveland. It receives roughly 4% of all state appropriations to higher education, which equates to a good $5,323 per student in fiscal 1996.

Like other Ohio public universities, Cleveland State experienced flat appropriations in the early 1990s, but support rose in fiscals 1995 and 1996, and the university is guaranteed a minimum of 3% for fiscal 1997.

Financial performance also improved, with good bottom lines of 5.8% and 4.9% in fiscals 1995 and 1996, respectively, or $6.8 million and $5.9 million on a nominal basis. This improvement allowed the university to grow its unrestricted moneys to $19.1 million, or 15.7% of unrestricted current fund operations, up from 6.3% in fiscal 1994.

Offsetting Cleveland State's improved financial performance is a significant drop in recent headcount enrollment. Since fiscal 1993, headcount enrollment has dropped by 2,500 students, with an additional 2% drop for fiscal 1997.

Current headcount of 15,671 and full time equivalent enrollment of 11,039 actually places the university in the mid-range for size in Ohio's higher education hierarchy. Student admissions are open and historically over half of all accepted students matriculate at the university.
More transfer students matriculate each year as new students than freshmen, as students attending community colleges can easily transfer to the state's four-year institutions.

The school's competitive law school enrolls an additional 900 students, although enrollment is expected to decline slightly. Most of Cleveland State's students are drawn directly from the metropolitan area, and the university houses only 550 students on campus.

Bond proceeds will be used to refinance outstanding BANs used to construct a parking garage on campus and complete the costs of a small parking project. The university has no other near-term debt plans.
The outlook anticipates a leveling of enrollment and modest increases in state support. Continued improvement in financial performance could be viewed positively, Standard & Poor's said.
